questions.question: Which of the following species is neither hypervalent nor hypovalent?
questions.explanation:
1. ClO₄⁻: Cl has 7 valence electrons. In ClO₄⁻, Cl forms 4 bonds (often depicted as double bonds for formal charge minimization), giving it effectively more than 8 electrons. (Hypervalent)
2. BCl₃: B has 3 valence electrons. In BCl₃, B forms 3 bonds, giving it only 6 valence electrons. (Hypovalent)
3. SO₄²⁻: S has 6 valence electrons. In SO₄²⁻, S forms 4 bonds (often depicted as double bonds for formal charge minimization), giving it effectively more than 8 electrons. (Hypervalent)   
4. CO₃²⁻: C has 4 valence electrons. In CO₃²⁻, C forms 4 bonds (one double, two single), giving it exactly 8 valence electrons.
Answer option 4,(CO₃²⁻).

questions.explanation:
Explanation
• Sigma (σ) bonds are formed by head-on overlap along the internuclear axis. Pi (π) bonds are formed by sideways overlap of atomic orbitals perpendicular to the internuclear axis.
Concept
• Internuclear axis is X. This means the bond is forming along the X-axis.
• (1) px + px along X-axis: This results in head-on overlap, forming a σ bond, not a π bond.
• (2) px + dxz along X-axis: The px orbital is along the X-axis. The dxz orbital has lobes in the XZ plane. Sideways overlap is not possible, forming a σ bond.
• (3) py + dxy along X-axis: The py orbital is along the Y-axis. The dxy orbital has lobes between the X and Y axes. Sideways overlap is possible, forming a π bond.
• (4) s + pz along X-axis: The s orbital is spherical. The pz orbital is along the Z-axis. There will be no effective sideways overlap to form a π bond along the X-axis. forming a σ bond, not a π bond.
Answer option 3

Which one of the following statements is incorrect  related to Molecular Orbital Theory ?
options: The π* antibonding molecular orbital has a node between the nuclei.
In the formation of bonding molecular orbital, the two electron waves of the bonding atoms reinforce each other.
Molecular orbitals obtained from 2px and 2py orbitals are symmetrical around the bond axis.
A π-bonding molecular orbital has larger electron density above and below the internuclear axis.
questions.explanation:
Solution/Explanation:
1. The π* antibonding molecular orbital has a node between the nuclei: This statement is correct. Antibonding orbitals, including π* orbital have a node between the nuclei, indicating destructive interference. 
2. In the formation of bonding molecular orbital, the two electron waves of the bonding atoms reinforce each other: This statement is also correct. Bonding orbitals are formed by constructive interference, leading to increased electron density between the nuclei. 
3. Molecular orbitals obtained from 2Px and 2Py orbitals are symmetrical around the bond axis: This statement is incorrect. Molecular orbitals formed from 2Px and 2Py orbitals are π orbitals, which are not symmetrical around the bond axis. Sigma (σ) orbitals are symmetrical around the bond axis. 
4. A π-bonding molecular orbital has larger electron density above and below the internuclear axis: This statement is correct. Pi (π) bonds are characterized by electron density above and below the internuclear axis. 
Therefore, the incorrect statement is:
Answer : Option : 3
